newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan ministry to sell off Big Three bank stakes.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan ministry to sell off Big Three bank stakes.

text.p: Taiwan's finance ministry said on Monday it would sell off its holdings in the island's "Big Three" state commercial banks by July 1997 to alleviate the government's budget deficit.
The ministry holds only small stakes in Chang Hwa, First Bank and Hua Nan, which are controlled by Taiwan's provincial government and will remain in state hands after the finance ministry selloff.
"This a budget passed by parliament to sell all of the ministry's holdings on the big three banks by June 30, 1997," a ministry official told Reuters.
"If it goes smoothly as planned, we will raise T$3.7 billion through the sales," he said.

The sale involves 20.55 million shares altogether -- 8.87 million shares of Chang Hwa, or 0.54 percent of the bank, 10.44 million shares or 0.58 percent of First Bank and 1.24 million shares or 0.06 percent of Hua Nan.
The budgeted selloff can be postponed for up to five years under law if the shares' market prices are not attractive at the time of the planned sales, he said.
The ministry may stagger the sales to reduce the impact on the stock market, the official said.

The ministry plans to sell T$1.837 billion of First Bank shares at T$176 per share, T$233 million worth of Hua Nan at T$188 and T$1.632 billion worth of Chang Hwa at T$184, he said, noting that the prices would act as references only.
The government, squeezed by a tax revenue shortfall amid a slow economy in the first three quarters, has forecast a fiscal 1996/97 (July/June) deficit of T$87.6 billion, he said.
